# [PR #2262] UTILS/FILE: Optimize query function.

source: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2262
state: open | updated: 2026-09-23T19:54:04Z
labels: external-contribution, size/L

## 正文

## What?

 * Optimize file query by removing redundant allocations and string copies.
 * Change the bulk query function to directly return a vector of results.
 * Remove the (previously outdated) documentation and redundant comments.
 * Change the gtest to create temporary files in `/tmp` instead of `/opt/nixl`.

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-22

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `Clang Format Check` · commit `5d8d5253`

**TL;DR:** The Clang Format Check failed on a single style violation — a stray blank line before the closing brace of `nixlGdsEngine::queryMem` in `src/plugins/cuda_gds/gds_backend.cpp`. Delete the blank line at line 412 (or run `clang-format-19 -i` on the file) and the check passes.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** GitHub Actions job `clang-format` (run 35727932645, PR #2262) exited 1 because `clang-format-diff-19` reported a formatting diff in the PR's changed lines.

**Root cause:** Not an infrastructure or tooling problem. The workflow step ran `git diff -U0 HEAD^1 HEAD -- $FILES | clang-format-diff-19 -p1 -style=file`, and clang-format proposed a change, which makes the step exit non-zero. The only reported violation is in `src/plugins/cuda_gds/gds_backend.cpp`:

```
@@ -409,5 +409,4 @@
 nixlGdsEngine::queryMem(const nixl_reg_dlist_t &descs, std::vector<nixl_query_resp_t> &resp) const {
     resp = nixl::queryFileInfoFromDescList(descs);
     return NIXL_SUCCESS;
-
-}
+}
```

Reading the source confirms it: line 411 is `return NIXL_SUCCESS;`, line 412 is an empty line, and line 413 is the closing `}`. The repo `.clang-format` style disallows a blank line immediately before a closing brace, so clang-format removes it. All other modified C/C++ files in the PR were clean.

**Implicated commit:** [REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String] — "Review comments." by Colin Hirsch (the PR head commit; it is the most recent change to this file and introduced the stray blank line)

**File:** src/plugins/cuda_gds/gds_backend.cpp:412

**Suggested fix:** Remove the empty line 412 so the function reads:

```cpp
nixl_status_t
nixlGdsEngine::queryMem(const nixl_reg_dlist_t &descs, std::vector<nixl_query_resp_t> &resp) const {
    resp = nixl::queryFileInfoFromDescList(descs);
    return NIXL_SUCCESS;
}
```

Easiest mechanical route: `clang-format-19 -i -style=file src/plugins/cuda_gds/gds_backend.cpp`, then amend/push. To catch this before pushing in future, wire the same clang-format invocation into a pre-commit hook.

**Related:** none — PR #2262 / run 35727932645 is the only occurrence; no existing issue matches this signature.

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `fe78fc8d`

**TL;DR:** The aarch64 "Build" variant failed in `meson setup` because the `taskflow` subproject is fetched with a live `git clone` from github.com, which failed on that agent (`fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address`); switch `subprojects/taskflow.wrap` from `[wrap-git]` to a tarball `[wrap-file]` (as liburing/tomlplusplus already do) so it is downloadable/cacheable and cannot hit a git auth prompt.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage `Build` (node 407, aarch64 variant) of `nixl-ci-non-gpu` #3148 aborted after 12.6 s with `meson.build:233:16: ERROR: Git command failed: ['/usr/bin/git', ... 'clone', '--depth','1','--branch','v3.10.0','https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git','taskflow']`.

**Root cause:** Dependency acquisition, not compiled code. `meson.build:233` resolves `taskflow` via a wrap fallback, and `subprojects/taskflow.wrap` is a `[wrap-git]` entry pointing at `https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git`. On the aarch64 agent that clone got an interactive credential prompt instead of anonymous access:
```
Cloning into 'taskflow'...
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
fatal: expected flush after ref listing
```
Meson later re-tried the fallback and errored out, killing the whole parallel stage. This is agent/network-side (GitHub smart-HTTP returned an auth challenge — typical of anonymous rate-limiting or a proxy intercept), not a defect in commit fe78fc8d: the same commit's x86_64 variant (stage 402) cloned taskflow successfully in ~12 s (`Dependency taskflow from subproject subprojects/taskflow found: YES 3.10.0`), and all five other Build/Test stages passed. Note the same aarch64 job *did* successfully fetch `liburing` over plain HTTPS (`Downloading liburing source from https://github.com/axboe/liburing/...tar.gz`), so the tarball path worked while only the git-protocol clone failed. The build is also fragile by design here: a `wrap-git` clone has no retry, no fallback and no tarball cache, so one transient GitHub hiccup fails the whole matrix leg.

**Implicated commit:** 76275cfc "Use tagged Taskflow git wrap for NIXL builds (#2121)" — bzsuni (introduced the `[wrap-git]` fetch; the trigger itself is infrastructural, not fe78fc8d)

**File:** `subprojects/taskflow.wrap:1-4` (consumed at `meson.build:233`)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Convert taskflow to a tarball wrap so it behaves like the other subprojects that succeeded on this agent:
```
[wrap-file]
directory = taskflow-3.10.0
source_url = https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow/archive/refs/tags/v3.10.0.tar.gz
source_filename = taskflow-3.10.0.tar.gz
source_hash = <sha256 of the tarball>
patch_directory = taskflow
[provide]
taskflow = taskflow_dep
```
   This is deterministic (hash-pinned), works with meson's wrap cache/`--wrap-mode`, and never triggers a git credential prompt.
2. As a hardening measure, export `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/true` in the CI build script so a failing clone errors immediately instead of blocking on a prompt, and consider pre-populating `subprojects/packagecache` (or a local GitHub mirror) in the CI images so dependency fetches don't depend on outbound GitHub availability per build.
3. Re-run build #3148 — the failure is not reproducible from the commit under test and should pass on retry.

**Related:** PR #2121 (introduced the taskflow git wrap); no existing issue tracks this clone flake — worth opening one for "pin subprojects to tarball wraps / pre-seed packagecache in CI images".

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `b8a23b4e`

**TL;DR:** 15 `prometheusTelemetryTest` cases failed in one of the six parallel non-GPU variants because `libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so` was never built there (the `prometheus-cpp` CMake/git subproject wasn't found), yet `test/gtest/meson.build` compiles and runs the Prometheus tests unconditionally — gate those sources on Prometheus availability (or `GTEST_SKIP` when the plugin is absent).

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage 449 ("Test CPP", one of six parallel matrix legs) failed: `gtest` reported 15/224 failures, all in `prometheusTelemetryTest` (`telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp`, `telemetry_histogram_test.cpp`), each with `Plugin file does not exist: .../libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so` → `Expected: (handle) != (nullptr)` / `Failed to load telemetry plugin: prometheus` (exit code 42).

**Root cause:** In that variant the Prometheus exporter plugin was not produced by the build. The matching Build stage (node 398) install list shows only `src/plugins/telemetry/doca/libtelemetry_exporter_doca.so` being installed into `/opt/nixl/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/plugins` — no `libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so`. `src/plugins/telemetry/prometheus/meson.build:36` pulls prometheus-cpp via `cmake.subproject('prometheus-cpp', required: false)` backed by a `wrap-git` (`subprojects/prometheus-cpp.wrap`, `clone-recursive = true`, github.com), so when that clone/configure fails the build only emits a warning and silently skips the plugin. Corroborating evidence from the same test log: the `telemetry_mp_collector`/`telemetry_mp_exporter`/`telemetry_mp_e2e` tests never ran in this variant (only `MpStoreTest.*` appears), which is exactly what happens when `nixl_telemetry_mp_collector_dep` / `nixl_telemetry_mp_exporter_dep` are undefined — i.e. prometheus-cpp was absent. Those prometheus_mp tests are correctly gated with `is_variable(...)` in `test/gtest/meson.build:142-156`, but `telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp` (line 112), `telemetry_prometheus_stress_test.cpp` (line 115) and the Prometheus cases in `telemetry_histogram_test.cpp` (line 114) are added unconditionally, so they hard-fail instead of being skipped. The tests are unrelated to the PR's change (commit b8a23b4e, branch `query_file`); the five other variants passed all 224 tests.

**Implicated commit:** unknown — not a regression from b8a23b4e; the gating gap dates back to the Prometheus exporter test introduction (b8ca6d80, alexanderbilk, "Prometheus telemetry exporter (#1091)") and was not fixed when the prometheus_mp tests were gated (407b69b6 / e1cbabca, e-eygin).

**File:** `test/gtest/meson.build:112` (unconditional `telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp`; also lines 114-115), plugin gate at `src/plugins/telemetry/prometheus/meson.build:36-59`; failing assertions at `test/gtest/telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp:157,233,288,352,387,430,544,561` and `test/gtest/telemetry_histogram_test.cpp:112,153`.

**Suggested fix:**
1. Make the test build follow the plugin build. `prometheus_found` from `src/plugins/telemetry/prometheus/meson.build` is visible in the project scope, so guard the sources:
   ```meson
   if is_variable('prometheus_found') and prometheus_found
       gtest_sources += ['telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp',
                         'telemetry_prometheus_stress_test.cpp',
                         'telemetry_histogram_test.cpp']
   endif
   ```
   (consistent with the existing `is_variable('nixl_telemetry_mp_collector_dep')` pattern). Alternatively, have the fixture `GTEST_SKIP() << "prometheus exporter plugin not built"` when `loadTelemetryPlugin("prometheus")` returns nullptr, so the suite degrades to SKIPPED rather than FAILED.
2. Separately, stop the silent skip from being invisible in CI: since the leg clearly *expects* Prometheus, either vendor/pre-install prometheus-cpp in that variant's Docker image (avoiding the network `wrap-git` clone-recursive at configure time) or pass `-Dforce_fallback_for=` / make it a hard `error()` when telemetry Prometheus is explicitly requested, so a failed subproject fetch fails the Build stage with a clear message instead of surfacing as 15 mystery test failures.
3. Re-run the build to confirm it is the transient subproject fetch — the other five variants built the plugin fine on the same commit.

**Related:** none

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` · commit `b8a23b4e`

**TL;DR:** The build compiled fine; it failed because the Slurm allocation on the DL cluster never got a node — `salloc` sat queued for the full `--immediate=3600` (60 min) window in partition `gb200nvl72_cx8` and exited with "Unable to allocate resources: Connection timed out". This is a cluster-capacity/infra failure, not a code defect in PR #2262; retrigger the build or get capacity/reservation on that partition.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage "Allocate DL EP Environment" (node 156) failed after 3,609 s when `salloc` on `dlcluster.nvidia.com` could not obtain a node in partition `gb200nvl72_cx8`.

**Root cause:** From the stage log, the pipeline invoked:
`salloc -N 1 -p gb200nvl72_cx8 --job-name=nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep-1278 --immediate=3600 --time=02:00:00 --no-shell --account=blackwell`
Slurm accepted it as **pending job allocation 2282339** (`job 2282339 queued and waiting for resources`) and then, after the 3600 s `--immediate` budget expired, returned `salloc: error: Unable to allocate resources: Connection timed out`, exit code 1, which aborted the parallel branch `build_helper_dl_ep/aarch64/1`.

Importantly this is *not* a hang in nixl code: the one-hour gap between `16:10:58` and `17:11:06` is the Slurm queue wait, and Slurm itself terminated the wait at its configured deadline. Everything before it succeeded — UCX install, meson configure, `ninja` 290/290 targets, nixlbench build, and the container push of `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep-test:1278` all completed by 16:10:46 (stage 141 "Compiling NIXL EP Docker Image for DL" = success). No compile or test error appears anywhere in the log; the only non-fatal noise is cosmetic (doxygen `HTML_EXTRA_FILES` missing `docs/doxygen/nixl.png`, and `cuObjClient not found` warnings), none of which affect the exit status.

Also note `salloc: lua: Setting job to exclusive mode as no gpu count was specified` — the job cluster's Lua submit plugin promoted the request to whole-node exclusive because no `--gpus`/`--gres` was passed. On a contended GB200 NVL72 partition, an exclusive whole-node request is markedly harder to schedule than a partial-GPU one, which plausibly contributed to the hour-long queue.

**Implicated commit:** none — the failure is independent of commit [REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]. The Slurm allocation parameters were last touched around c984ce65 (lishapira, "CI: add vLLM + NIXL EP test to the EP CI job", #2154), which introduced this EP job's allocation step.

**File:** the `slurm.allocation` call for `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` (args logged at stage 156: `partition:gb200nvl72_cx8, immediateTimeout:3600, jobTimeout:02:00:00, extraArgs:[--account=blackwell]`) — in the `.ci/jenkins/pipeline` job definition for this job; the implementation lives in the external `swx-jenkins-lib` shared library.

**Suggested fix:** Retrigger build #1278 — nothing in the PR needs changing. To reduce recurrence: (1) ask the DL cluster admins about `blackwell`-account backlog on `gb200nvl72_cx8` around 2026-09-23 16:10–17:11 UTC, quoting pending allocation **2282339**, and consider a CI reservation or higher QoS priority; (2) specify an explicit `--gpus`/`--gres` count in `extraArgs` so the Lua plugin does not force exclusive whole-node mode, which should schedule faster; (3) make the allocation step resilient rather than fatal — retry the `salloc` a couple of times, and mark the build UNSTABLE/aborted (not FAILURE) when the failure is `Unable to allocate resources`, so capacity shortages are not reported as PR test failures. Do not simply raise `immediateTimeout`; the work was never running, so a longer wait only lengthens the queue-blocked build.

**Related:** none — searches for this allocation error returned only unrelated EP/telemetry PRs (#2248, #2153, #2070).
